VALENCIA's reference centroids

Source: R/valencia.r
valencia_centroids.Rd

The 13 reference centroids of VALENCIA (France et al. 2020), against which valencia() classifies vaginal microbiome samples: the mean relative abundances of 199 taxa in the reference samples of each sub-CST.

Usage

valencia_centroids

Format

A numeric matrix of 13 sub-CSTs (rows: "I-A", "I-B", "II", "III-A", "III-B", "IV-A", "IV-B", "IV-C0" to "IV-C4", "V") \(\times\) 199 taxa (columns, named as VALENCIA names them; see valencia()). Each row sums to 1, to rounding.

Source

CST_centroids_012920.csv from VALENCIA, commit 8559d45 of https://github.com/ravel-lab/VALENCIA, built by data-raw/valencia_centroids.r in ecodive's source repository. Released under the MIT licence:

Details

The centroids were computed from 13,160 taxonomic profiles of 1,975 North American women, from 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing; only these means are included, no individual data. A revised set of centroids (for instance with all Prevotella merged into "g_Prevotella", and the samples' taxa merged the same way) can be given to valencia() as its centroids.

References

France, M. T., Ma, B., Gajer, P., Brown, S., Humphrys, M. S., Holm, J. B., Waetjen, L. E., Brotman, R. M., & Ravel, J. (2020). VALENCIA: a nearest centroid classification method for vaginal microbial communities based on composition. Microbiome, 8, 166. doi:10.1186/s40168-020-00934-6

See also

valencia()

    dim(valencia_centroids)
#> [1]  13 199
    round(valencia_centroids[, 1:5], 3)
